facts.description: Create new memories during customizable animal encounters at Helen Woodward Animal Center! This animal education opportunity is a perfect activity for any animal lover and works well with playgroups, youth groups, 4H groups, home school groups, families, and retirement homes. You will not only get hands-on animal interactions but will also gain a better understanding of our furred, feathered, and scaled friends. Program defaults as 60-minute but you can select the 'extra time program' per participant to extend it to a 90-minute program for even more fun! A minimum of 6 participants is required to make this booking. You may bring less participants on the day of the program, but we will not refund the difference if less than 6 participants attend, as that is the minimum cost we need to run the program.

facts.description: Interacting with animals is a fun and unique way for students to learn about the world around them. We offer a variety of programs that give kids in San Diego the chance to meet cute critters while learning lessons that complement their grade level's NGSS and incorporate STEM. Year-round field trips to the Center or outreaches to your classroom are offered for preschool, elementary, middle and high school classes. If you are a school, please call us at 858-756-4117 ext 318 or email us at education@animalcenter.org to reserve your spot, this way we can book you without upfront payment, and then we will invoice you at the time of program completion to get an accurate and final headcount.
facts.detailsText: We are looking forward to seeing you! Education Outreaches include animal encounters and interactive educational activities that meet grade-level STEM and NGSS. - If you chose the 60-minute version and did not select STEM as part of our time with you, we should leave paperwork copies for each teacher which explains the STEM activity we would have done and provides a template if applicable. If you did not receive this, please email us and we can send it electronically to you. - Some of our STEM activities include follow-up activities for the class to complete after we leave, if the teacher so desires. We will leave paperwork copies for each teacher which explains the follow up activity and provides any applicable templates. If you did not receive this and believe you should have, please email us and we can send it electronically to you if applicable. - - - CLASSROOM EXPECTATIONS - We will arrive ~15 minutes before the start time to check in, set up our equipment, and let the animals get used to their surroundings. It is very helpful if we can set up before the children are present. - Please inform us before the visit where we should park if there are special instructions. It is easier to unload our vehicle if we can park close to the building. We can move our vehicle after we unload if necessary. - An indoor area where the students can sit comfortably in a half circle so everyone can easily see is required. If an outdoors location is the only option, it limits our animals to only reptiles and invertebrates for animal safety purposes. - Remaining in the same location throughout the visit and having each class come to us is necessary. This reduces stress on the animals and helps us stay on time as we bring many supplies with us that are difficult to keep packing/unpacking between classes. - In order to best serve the students and maintain animal health and safety, we only present to one class at a time (20-30 students maximum). - Our staff are trained on positive classroom management strategies, but we appreciate continued support from the teacher to ensure the best experience for the children and the animals. We will check in at the office and head to the designated room to await your class' arrival. We will check in at the office and head to the designated room to await your class' arrival. facts.description: Spring Adventure is an engaging, seasonally themed program that invites children to explore the science of spring through animals, observation, and hands-on learning. Participants will meet live animal ambassadors-including a mammal, bird, amphibian, and invertebrate-take part in an age-appropriate STEM activity focused on butterfly conservation, and learn about life cycles, baby animals, and the changes plants and animals experience as winter turns to spring. The program encourages curiosity, critical thinking, and compassion for animals while reinforcing foundational science concepts in a fun, accessible way. Schools: Spring Adventure incorporates STEM concepts and aligns with Next Generation Science Standards for grades K-6. The program can be hosted on-site at our campus or brought directly to your classroom to reduce transportation costs and simplify scheduling. Schools are encouraged to call or email our Education Office to book; this allows us to reserve your program without upfront payment and invoice after the program concludes. Girl Scouts: this program can be customized to meet some of the “Between Earth and Sky” journey requirements for Daisies.
facts.detailsText: We are looking forward to seeing you! CHECK-IN PROCEDURE Meet at Education lobby to check in, at which point you will be directed back to the main meeting space for your program at one of our indoor classrooms or playgrounds. PROGRAM EXPECTATIONS To prepare children for live animal presentations at Helen Woodward Animal Center, please read and share the following before you arrive: All participants, regardless of age, should wear closed-toed shoes. Please remain with the group at all times. Some areas of the Center are restricted to staff access only. Food is only permitted in our Park or Pollinator event spaces. Not all animals can be pet. Your guide will invite you to pet when available. Animals are very sensitive to and easily startled by loud, high-pitched sounds and fast movement. Help children act respectfully around the animals by keeping "voices low and feet slow." For this reason flash photography is also prohibited. Our Instructors will be expecting your arrival, but may not immediately be out there to greet you if they are finishing room and animal preparation, especially if you arrive early.
